what_happened: The person running Athena had set themselves a limit of two jobs at once. A two-job batch was already running, and they started their stale-work retry next to it, counting the batch as one job. Two writer builds of 12 to 13 GB each took free disk down to 2 GB. They stopped the retry and deleted its build folder. No job is recorded as failed. This is the second time they ran the retry beside the batch.
cause: Athena does not tie parallel job starts to disk. A hand-started job is not checked against the number of jobs already running or against free disk minus the combined build size of running jobs plus the new one. The concurrency limit is a number the person keeps in their head. Athena shows neither the running count nor the expected disk need, so a person miscounts and a repeated mistake is not stopped. The low-disk guard acts only after disk has fallen.
prevention: Add a start-time check to every path that starts a job, including hand starts. It counts the jobs actually running, including every job in a running batch. It refuses the start, naming the running jobs, when the count is at max_concurrency. It also refuses when free disk minus the estimated build size (about 13 GB per producer build) of the running jobs plus the new one would drop below the guard floor. It prints the running count, free disk and estimate, and allows an explicit override that is logged.
proposed_request: Add a pre-start capacity check to every Athena command that starts a job (drain, retry, run and approve-work), including hand starts while a drain or batch is running. Before starting, count the jobs currently running, including each job in a running batch, and read free disk. Refuse the start, naming the running jobs, if the count is already at max_concurrency, or if free disk minus 13 GB for each running producer build and for the new job would fall below the free-disk guard floor. When it refuses, print the running count, the free disk and the estimated need. Allow an explicit override flag that is recorded as an intervention. Acceptance: (1) with a two-job batch running and max_concurrency = 2, a hand-started retry is refused with a message naming both running jobs; (2) with one job running and free disk too low for two builds, the start is refused and prints the numbers; (3) with enough room the start proceeds unchanged; (4) the override is allowed and recorded; (5) tests cover the serial path (max_concurrency = 1) and the parallel path.
